question: On a hydraulic grade line plot for a pressure zone, which two values are added together at a junction to locate the grade line height?
correctAnswer: Elevation head plus pressure head at that point
explanation: The hydraulic grade line sits at the elevation head plus the pressure head at each point along the system.
options: Elevation head plus pressure head at that point
Velocity head plus friction loss in the main
Pump head plus the tank overflow elevation
Demand flow plus the static water level
optionA: Elevation head plus pressure head at that point
optionB: Velocity head plus friction loss in the main
optionC: Pump head plus the tank overflow elevation
optionD: Demand flow plus the static water level

question: A pressure reducing valve station includes a smaller bypass valve set slightly higher than the main valve. During low night flows, what does the bypass valve do?
correctAnswer: It carries the small flow so the large main valve stays seated
explanation: A small bypass PRV set a little higher opens first at low flow, passing small demands accurately while the large main valve remains closed until flow rises.
options: It closes the station so the zone is fed from storage only
It raises upstream pressure to protect the supply main
It carries the small flow so the large main valve stays seated
It drains the downstream zone to relieve excess pressure
optionA: It closes the station so the zone is fed from storage only
optionB: It raises upstream pressure to protect the supply main
optionC: It carries the small flow so the large main valve stays seated
optionD: It drains the downstream zone to relieve excess pressure

question: Before a district metered area can report trustworthy night flow, which setup step must be completed at its boundaries?
correctAnswer: All boundary valves are closed and confirmed tight shut
explanation: A DMA works only when inflow passes through its meter, so boundary valves must be closed and proven not to leak past before night flow data means anything.
options: All hydrants inside the area are painted and numbered
All boundary valves are closed and confirmed tight shut
All services inside the area are fitted with new meters
All mains inside the area are flushed in one direction
optionA: All hydrants inside the area are painted and numbered
optionB: All boundary valves are closed and confirmed tight shut
optionC: All services inside the area are fitted with new meters
optionD: All mains inside the area are flushed in one direction

question: On one graph, a pump curve and a system curve are plotted together. The duty point of the operating pump is located where?
correctAnswer: Where the two curves cross each other on the plot
explanation: The duty point is the intersection of the pump curve and the system curve, the one flow and head combination that satisfies both at the same time.
options: At the highest point reached by the pump curve
At the lowest point reached by the system curve
Where the system curve meets the flow axis alone
Where the two curves cross each other on the plot
optionA: At the highest point reached by the pump curve
optionB: At the lowest point reached by the system curve
optionC: Where the system curve meets the flow axis alone
optionD: Where the two curves cross each other on the plot

question: A storage tank operator tracks turnover by comparing daily inflow and outflow volumes. If inflow equals outflow for a week but the level never changes, what is the concern?
correctAnswer: The same water may sit in the tank while new water short circuits through it
explanation: Equal in and out volumes with a fixed level can mean short circuiting, where new water passes through and older water stays, so level movement is needed to confirm real turnover.
options: The same water may sit in the tank while new water short circuits through it
The tank overflow will run continuously during the whole week
The chlorine residual will rise because the water is too fresh
The tank foundation will be overloaded by the steady level
optionA: The same water may sit in the tank while new water short circuits through it
optionB: The tank overflow will run continuously during the whole week
optionC: The chlorine residual will rise because the water is too fresh
optionD: The tank foundation will be overloaded by the steady level

question: A chloraminated system watches nitrification start in warm storage. Which sample result is usually the earliest warning sign?
correctAnswer: A fall in free ammonia with a rise in nitrite levels
explanation: Nitrifying bacteria consume free ammonia and produce nitrite, so falling free ammonia together with rising nitrite is an early indicator before residuals collapse.
options: A rise in total chlorine with a fall in nitrite levels
A rise in water hardness with a fall in alkalinity
A fall in free ammonia with a rise in nitrite levels
A fall in turbidity with a rise in colour levels
optionA: A rise in total chlorine with a fall in nitrite levels
optionB: A rise in water hardness with a fall in alkalinity
optionC: A fall in free ammonia with a rise in nitrite levels
optionD: A fall in turbidity with a rise in colour levels
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Nitrification monitoring and response. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: In a valve exercising program, what is recorded each time a valve is operated?
correctAnswer: Turns to close, direction, condition and any defects found
explanation: Each exercise visit records turns, direction of operation, condition and defects so the next crew can find, operate and trust the valve in an emergency.
options: Only the valves that failed and could not be turned
Turns to close, direction, condition and any defects found
The names of customers who called about low pressure
The chlorine residual measured at the nearest hydrant
optionA: Only the valves that failed and could not be turned
optionB: Turns to close, direction, condition and any defects found
optionC: The names of customers who called about low pressure
optionD: The chlorine residual measured at the nearest hydrant

question: A large meter at a factory is selected for testing because its registered volume has dropped over two years while production stayed steady. What does a low flow test point check?
correctAnswer: Whether the meter still registers small flows accurately
explanation: Large meters are tested across their flow range, and the low flow point shows whether worn internals are letting small flows pass unregistered.
options: Whether the meter body can withstand full line pressure
Whether the meter dial can be read from street level
Whether the meter setting meets fire flow demands
Whether the meter still registers small flows accurately

question: Two neighbourhoods share one pressure zone fed from a tank with a water surface at 210 m. One area sits at 150 m elevation and the other at 175 m. With no flow in the mains, which statement about static pressure is correct?
correctAnswer: The lower area has more pressure head than the higher area
explanation: Static head is the tank level minus ground elevation: 60 m at the lower area and 35 m at the higher area, so the lower area carries more pressure head.
options: The lower area has more pressure head than the higher area
The higher area has more pressure head than the lower area
Both areas have exactly the same pressure head at all times
Static pressure head does not depend on ground elevation
optionA: The lower area has more pressure head than the higher area
optionB: The higher area has more pressure head than the lower area
optionC: Both areas have exactly the same pressure head at all times
optionD: Static pressure head does not depend on ground elevation

question: After a PRV station is rebuilt, downstream pressure creeps upward overnight even though demand is near zero. Which check comes first?
correctAnswer: Confirm the valve seat is not passing water when closed
explanation: Pressure creep at zero demand usually means the closed valve is passing water through a worn or fouled seat, so seat tightness is checked before settings are changed.
options: Replace the downstream pressure gauge with a new one
Raise the set point to match the creeping pressure
Confirm the valve seat is not passing water when closed
Open the bypass valve fully and leave it open overnight
optionA: Replace the downstream pressure gauge with a new one
optionB: Raise the set point to match the creeping pressure
optionC: Confirm the valve seat is not passing water when closed
optionD: Open the bypass valve fully and leave it open overnight

question: A DMA serving 900 homes shows minimum night flow climbing steadily for three weeks while daytime demand stays flat. What is the most likely explanation?
correctAnswer: A new leak or background losses are growing inside the district
explanation: Legitimate night use changes slowly, so a steady rise in minimum night flow with flat daytime demand points to growing leakage inside the district.
options: Customers inside the district are using less water at night
A new leak or background losses are growing inside the district
The district meter is reading lower than the true flow
Boundary valves have been opened to a neighbouring district
optionA: Customers inside the district are using less water at night
optionB: A new leak or background losses are growing inside the district
optionC: The district meter is reading lower than the true flow
optionD: Boundary valves have been opened to a neighbouring district

question: A booster pump runs further back on its curve each summer as a subdivision grows, delivering less flow at higher head. Which change to the system curve explains this?
correctAnswer: The system curve steepens because friction losses rise
explanation: Higher flows through the same mains raise friction loss, steepening the system curve, so its crossing with the pump curve moves to lower flow and higher head.
options: The system curve flattens because friction losses fall
The system curve disappears because demand is higher
The system curve shifts down because static lift falls
The system curve steepens because friction losses rise
optionA: The system curve flattens because friction losses fall
optionB: The system curve disappears because demand is higher
optionC: The system curve shifts down because static lift falls

question: A standpipe serves a small town and the bottom third never leaves the tank. Which operating change improves turnover of that stored water?
correctAnswer: Widen the fill and draw range so deeper water cycles daily
explanation: Cycling through a wider level range draws down the deeper stored water each day instead of repeatedly exchanging only the top layer.
options: Widen the fill and draw range so deeper water cycles daily
Keep the operating band narrow near the top of the tank
Add a second overflow pipe at the top of the tank wall
Paint the tank interior with a smoother coating finish
optionA: Widen the fill and draw range so deeper water cycles daily
optionB: Keep the operating band narrow near the top of the tank

question: Samples from a dead end main show nitrite present, free ammonia nearly gone and total chlorine falling week by week. Which response addresses the cause rather than the symptom?
correctAnswer: Flush the affected water out and review the chloramine feed balance
explanation: The pattern shows active nitrification, so removing the affected water by flushing and correcting the chlorine to ammonia feed balance treats the cause.
options: Add more sampling points along the dead end main
Lower the sample tap so it draws from the main invert
Flush the affected water out and review the chloramine feed balance
Record the results and wait for cooler weather to arrive

correctAnswer: Note the defect, schedule the valve for repair or replacement, and track it to completion
explanation: A valve that fails during an emergency must be logged as defective, scheduled for repair or replacement, and tracked until it is returned to reliable service.
options: Remove the valve from the system map so crews stop trying to use it
Note the defect, schedule the valve for repair or replacement, and track it to completion
Leave the valve as found and record nothing so the map stays simple
Transfer the valve to the hydrant program for checking next season

question: Test results show a compound meter under registers at low flows but is accurate at high flows. Which part of the meter is the likely problem?
correctAnswer: The small positive displacement element for low flows
explanation: In a compound meter the small displacement element measures low flows, so low flow under registration with good high flow accuracy points to that element.

The register head that totals both measuring elements
The strainer basket installed ahead of the meter body
The small positive displacement element for low flows

question: A hydraulic model shows the grade line dropping steeply along one long main during peak hour while other mains drop gently. What does the steep drop tell the operator?
correctAnswer: That main is carrying flow with high friction loss per length
explanation: The slope of the hydraulic grade line is the friction loss per unit length, so a steep slope marks a main losing head quickly as it carries flow.
options: That main is carrying flow with high friction loss per length
That main is oversized for the flow it carries each day
That main is leaking at a steady rate along its length
That main is being fed from two directions at once

question: A hillside zone is fed through one PRV. Residents at the bottom report pressure above the target range on quiet nights. Which adjustment fits the cause?
correctAnswer: Lower the PRV set point or add night time pressure control
explanation: At low night demand, friction loss nearly disappears and downstream pressure rises toward the set point, so lowering the setting or using night control trims the excess.
options: Raise the PRV set point so daytime pressure improves
Install a larger PRV body so more flow can pass through
Lower the PRV set point or add night time pressure control
Remove the strainer so the valve responds more quickly

question: Step testing inside a DMA closes sections one at a time at night and watches the district meter. A large flow drop when one section closes tells the crew what?
correctAnswer: That section holds a large share of the night losses
explanation: In a step test, the size of the flow drop when a section is isolated shows how much of the night flow, and likely the leakage, sits in that section.
options: That section has the newest pipes in the whole district
That section holds a large share of the night losses
That section should be removed from the district meter
That section is fed from a different pressure zone

question: A pump that once met peak demand now cavitates near its duty point after years of main tuberculation. What has changed in the system?
correctAnswer: Friction losses have risen so suction conditions worsened
explanation: Tuberculation narrows and roughens mains, raising friction loss and reducing suction pressure at the pump, which can push operation into cavitation.
options: Static lift has fallen so the pump runs too far right
The impeller has grown larger from years of service wear
The system curve has flattened below the pump curve
Friction losses have risen so suction conditions worsened
optionA: Static lift has fallen so the pump runs too far right
optionB: The impeller has grown larger from years of service wear
optionC: The system curve has flattened below the pump curve

question: Two identical tanks feed one zone. Tank A cycles through 40 percent of its volume daily while Tank B cycles through 5 percent. Which action balances turnover between them?
correctAnswer: Adjust altitude valves or controls so Tank B fills and draws more
explanation: Unequal cycling usually reflects control settings, so adjusting altitude valves or level controls makes the lazy tank share filling and drawing duty.

Raise both tank levels to their overflow elevations
Take Tank A out of service until Tank B catches up fully
Lower the zone pressure so both tanks drain more slowly

question: A utility boosts chloramine residual leaving the plant during a nitrification episode but results in the far zone keep worsening. Why can boosting alone fail?
correctAnswer: Nitrifying bacteria in the system consume the added residual locally
explanation: Established nitrifying bacteria in biofilm and sediment consume added chloramine where they live, so boosting without flushing and feed correction often fails to recover the zone.
options: Added chloramine converts instantly to free chlorine in the mains
Boosting raises nitrite so fast that sampling cannot track it
Nitrifying bacteria in the system consume the added residual locally
Chloramine cannot travel beyond the first kilometre of main

question: A hydrant program finds the same hydrant dry barrel holding water on two yearly visits. What is the operational risk if this is left uncorrected through winter?
correctAnswer: Trapped water can freeze and crack the hydrant barrel
explanation: A barrel that does not drain leaves water trapped above the drain, and freezing can crack the barrel and put the hydrant out of service when it is needed.
options: The hydrant paint will fade faster in cold weather
Trapped water can freeze and crack the hydrant barrel
The hydrant caps will become too tight to remove by hand
The hydrant flow rating will increase beyond its class

optionB: Trapped water can freeze and crack the hydrant barrel

question: During a fire flow event, pressure at a hydrant falls sharply while the tank level barely changes. Which component of head is being consumed?

Elevation head between the tank and the hydrant site
Pressure head stored in the tank water surface level
Velocity head inside the hydrant barrel and outlet

question: A PRV station feeds a zone where a hospital needs firm pressure, but old services at low elevation burst on quiet nights. Which control strategy balances both needs?
correctAnswer: Flow modulated control that lowers pressure when demand is low

A bypass line left open so the zone follows upstream pressure
Flow modulated control that lowers pressure when demand is low
Weekly manual set point changes made by the day shift crew

question: A DMA night flow report shows leakage rising, but a boundary valve was found passing 3 L/s into the district last week. How should the crew treat the leakage figure?
correctAnswer: Correct for the passing valve before judging district leakage

Correct for the passing valve before judging district leakage
Discard all night flow data collected for the full year
Subtract the daytime average demand from the night flow

question: A reservoir with a common inlet and outlet develops persistent low residual at the far wall despite good average turnover figures. Which diagnosis fits best?
correctAnswer: Flow short circuits between inlet and outlet, leaving the far water old
explanation: Good averages can hide short circuiting, where water travels directly from inlet to outlet and the far side of the reservoir ages without exchanging.

The whole reservoir volume is simply too large for the town
The reservoir roof vents are letting chlorine escape to air
The outlet valve is oversized for the daily demand flow

question: Free ammonia in a chloraminated zone has fallen for a month, nitrite is detectable at three sites and residuals are dropping fastest near a warm tank. Which combined response is strongest?

explanation: An established episode needs the nitrified water removed, the warm storage cycled, and the chlorine to ammonia balance corrected together; monitoring alone lets it grow.

Switch the whole system to free chlorine permanently without notice
Flush the affected area, draw down and cycle the tank, and correct the feed ratio
Lower the tank level once and return to the normal program

question: Budget allows exercising either every valve every five years or critical valves yearly and the rest on a longer cycle. Which program design protects emergency isolation best?
correctAnswer: Prioritize critical isolation valves yearly and keep a longer cycle for the rest

options: Exercise every valve on the same five year cycle evenly
Prioritize critical isolation valves yearly and keep a longer cycle for the rest

Exercise hydrant valves only, since main valves rarely fail

correctAnswer: Test the school meter, because low flow under registration hides there

question: A distribution pump running at 1750 rpm delivers a head of 50 m. The speed is reduced to 1400 rpm for night operation. Using the affinity laws, where head varies with the square of the speed ratio, what head does the pump deliver at the lower speed? Round to 0 decimal places.
explanation: H2 = H1 x (N2/N1)^2. Substitute the stated values: 50 x (1400/1750) x (1400/1750) = 50 x 0.64 = 32 m. Round only the final result to 0 decimal places.

question: A district metered area records a minimum night flow of 18 L/s, of which legitimate night use accounts for 4 L/s. The night period lasts 6 hours. What volume of water is lost to leakage during that night period? Use 3600 seconds per hour and 1000 L per m3. Round to 1 decimal place.

question: A pump delivers 80 L/s at a head of 36 m. Demand growth requires the same pump, sped up, to deliver 100 L/s. Using the affinity laws, where flow varies directly with speed and head varies with the square of the speed ratio, what head will the pump deliver at the new speed? Round to 2 decimal places.
explanation: H2 = H1 x (Q2/Q1)^2, since the speed ratio equals the flow ratio. Substitute the stated values: 36 x (100/80) x (100/80) = 36 x 1.5625 = 56.25 m. Round only the final result to 2 decimal places.

question: A zone inlet holds a pressure head of 58 m. Water travels through 3500 m of main losing head at a given rate of 3.6 m per 1000 m, rises 8 m in elevation, and passes fittings that lose a further 1.4 m. What pressure remains at the far end, expressed in kPa? Use 9.81 kPa per metre of head. Round to 2 decimal places.
explanation: Remaining pressure = (inlet head - friction - rise - minor losses) x 9.81. Substitute the stated values: friction is 3.6 x 3500/1000 = 12.6 m, leaving 58 - 12.6 - 8 - 1.4 = 36.0 m, and 36.0 x 9.81 = 353.16 kPa. Round only the final result to 2 decimal places.
